Catch.Comment: config#6408 (Brian's 2026-08-04 operator ruling): Director failure is now TERMINAL — route to NormalizeFailureContext so the execution ends FAILED rather than reporting degraded success. The Director's Lambda error is captured at $.error (ResultPath) for HandleFailure's SNS alert.

CheckSkipAggregateCosts.Comment: Skip-gate. {"skip_aggregate_costs": true} bypasses the daily cost-telemetry aggregation Lambda (used for ad-hoc reruns where the cost parquet for the date is already current, or when iterating on the aggregator script). Standalone invocation of the Lambda is always available via the deploy.sh aggregate_costs target. POSITION (alpha-engine-config-I7194, 2026-08-25): this gate and the states behind it were the LAST states of ResearchPredictorParallel branch 0 until now. They sit at the TOP LEVEL, on the single edge every real-completion path takes into CheckShellRunNotify — after Director, the pipeline's most expensive LLM call. The entry point is this gate rather than DirectorComplete deliberately: DirectorComplete is entered ONLY via Director's success edge, so anchoring there would silently skip cost aggregation on {"skip_director": true}, on {"skip_post_eval": true} and on the ReportCard fail-open — exactly the reruns. Independent of skip_rationale_clustering / skip_counterfactual / skip_report_card / skip_director / skip_scanner_leaderboard / skip_post_eval: cost telemetry is not part of the post-eval advisory tail, and none of those flags has ever bypassed it.

AggregateCosts.Comment: Daily cost-telemetry aggregation Lambda. Reads decision_artifacts/_cost_raw/{run_date}/*.jsonl and writes the daily parquet at decision_artifacts/_cost/{run_date}/cost.parquet, emits per-agent CW metrics under AlphaEngine/Cost, and asserts FAN-IN COVERAGE (config-I7179): the set of distinct producers under _cost_raw must contain every producer the `coverage.required_producers` map below declares for the stages this execution actually entered, and must contain nothing outside the declared/conditional/allowed sets. A COUNT cannot see this defect — five Think Tank files look exactly like healthy coverage, which is what they were mistaken for until 2026-08-13. POSITION (alpha-engine-config-I7194, 2026-08-25): this state ran as the last state of ResearchPredictorParallel branch 0 until now, which put it BEFORE Director — the single most expensive LLM call in the pipeline, `ultra` group, callsite director-plan — so cost.parquet structurally could not contain the pipeline's largest cost and AlphaEngine/Cost under-reported by an unbounded margin in the reassuring direction. It now runs at the top level on the single edge into CheckShellRunNotify, after Director AND after the ScannerLeaderboard leaf, so every state that can emit a cost row has emitted it before the prefix is read. Director is consequently promoted from allowed_producers to required_producers, and its SECOND callsite — director-retro-judge (crucible-evaluator director/retro.py, run best-effort by the SAME Lambda invocation and genuinely absent on the first cycle, when there is no prior plan, and when the invocation budget is exhausted) — is declared CONDITIONAL: undeclared, it would arrive as a present-but-undeclared producer the moment the Director's IAM grant lands (alpha-engine-config-I8152) and the aggregator would refuse it. Failure is non-blocking (Catch routes to MarkAggregateCostsDegraded) — cost telemetry is observability, NOT a primary deliverable; a coverage breach must be loud without regressing the alpha pipeline. alpha-engine-config-I8335: evaljudge-shadow (crucible-research evals/judge.py::_call_openrouter_judge_llm via evaluate_artifact_openrouter) is declared ALLOWED, not required and not conditional, because NO state of this Step Function reaches it. Its only live invoker is lambda/openrouter_shadow_handler.py, fired by the standalone EventBridge rule alpha-research-openrouter-shadow-weekly (Sunday 10:00 UTC, crucible-research infrastructure/setup-openrouter-shadow-schedule.sh, which states verbatim that it is 'explicitly NOT a new state on the production Saturday ... chain'), and krepis S3JsonlCostSink partitions on each record's OWN ts, so a Sunday run lands in the Sunday prefix rather than in the Saturday $.run_date prefix this check reads. Declaring it CONDITIONAL under EvalJudgeProcess would key its admission on a stage that does not produce it — a false claim about the topology that would also stop admitting it the moment eval-judge is skipped. Same class as thinktank-*: an out-of-band producer sharing the prefix, allowed so it can never read as present-but-undeclared (a manual shadow re-run or a schedule move would otherwise trip the check on a declaration gap), never required because its absence says nothing about this pipeline. Status contract OK / SKIPPED / ERROR mirrors data #295 + L3277 audit. | alpha-engine-config-I8809: PARTITION FAMILY = trading_day - $.run_date is the cycle's trading day from NormalizeRunDates, and every artifact prefix and stage-coverage verdict this state produces keys off it. Downstream normalization with krepis.dates.resolve_trading_day is idempotent, so this is a no-op for consumers that already normalized and a convergence for those that did not. | alpha-engine-config-I10539 (Brian ruling 2026-09-16, option b): the ReplayConcordance stage is RETIRED. Its subject corpus — the six-team research agents (sector_quant, sector_qual, sector_peer_review, macro_economist, ic_cio, thesis_update) — was retired under alpha-engine-config-I1580 on 2026-07-20; the 56-day replay window slid past the last matching DecisionArtifact (2026-07-11) between the 2026-08-29 run (n_artifacts_candidate=46) and the 2026-09-05 run (0), and the zero-call run then failed the 2026-09-12 canonical weekly SF at AggregateCosts with CostCoverageError. A measurement stage exists only while its population exists. crucible-backtester replay/ and the alpha-engine-replay-concordance Lambda remain deployable standalone; only the weekly stage is gone. required_producers no longer declares replay-concordance: nothing in this definition invokes the concordance Lambda, so requiring its cost record is a demand for spend that cannot happen — the exact CostCoverageError that ended the 2026-09-12 run. It is NOT moved to allowed_producers: an out-of-band standalone invocation landing in this run_date's prefix SHOULD read as present-but-undeclared and refuse loudly.

Catch.Comment: Cost-telemetry aggregation is observability — failure must NOT halt the pipeline. The next Saturday SF will retry over a fresh _cost_raw partition; the prior week's parquet (or the manual-trigger fallback via scripts/aggregate_costs.py) remains available. alpha-engine-config#6722: this Catch matches sf-pipeline-policy.md §5's NAMED cost-aggregation carve-out verbatim ('Health-check and cost-aggregation stages may fail-open ... They must still set a degraded flag'). alpha-engine-config-I7194: the flag it sets is now $.aggregate_costs_degraded, its own top-level family, because the branch-local $.research_degraded_local this path used to thread exists only inside the Parallel and is hoisted as branch_a_degraded — which would attribute a cost-aggregation failure to a Parallel that no longer contains the aggregator.

MarkAggregateCostsDegraded.Comment: alpha-engine-config-I7194: the SF-controlled visible flag CheckGateDegradedNotify reads, set BEFORE the summary so the flag is on the execution record whatever happens downstream. Shape mirrors ScannerLeaderboardDegraded / ReportCardDegraded exactly. Replaces the branch-local $.research_degraded_local this Catch path set while the aggregator lived inside ResearchPredictorParallel branch 0.

SetAggregateCostsDegradedSummary.Comment: alpha-engine-config-I7194: mirrors SetScannerLeaderboardDegradedSummary. $.degraded_summary is what CheckDegradedOutcome reads to route to WriteCompletionMarkerDegraded — without it the run would end SUCCEEDED with no cost record for the cycle. Like every sibling Set*DegradedSummary in this definition it OVERWRITES an earlier stage's summary; the per-stage booleans survive independently. Deliberately carries NO stage_error: the sibling convention is uniform and a Choice path added later must not start throwing States.Runtime here (tests/test_degraded_terminal_derives_its_cause.py). Continuation is CheckShellRunNotify — the same edge the success and skip paths take, so a fail-open changes what the run SAYS, never where it goes. | alpha-engine-config-I8809: PARTITION FAMILY = trading_day (pass-through). This state does not KEY on the date; it carries $.run_date into a summary payload or a notification body. It is named here anyway because the contract test requires every state touching a run-date variable to state which family it means — an undeclared site is how the split reappeared once already.

PublishAggregateCostsDegraded.Comment: alpha-engine-config-I8336: named alert on the cost-aggregation fail-open path, mirroring PublishScannerLeaderboardDegraded's shape exactly (config#1819 discipline: hardcoded Subject/Message constants, never States.Format against unbounded input; best-effort Catch so a publish failure cannot block the path it decorates). Before this state the fail-open set $.aggregate_costs_degraded and walked straight to CheckShellRunNotify, so the ONLY signal was the terminal completion email — and $.aggregate_costs_degraded is registered LAST in CheckGateDegradedNotify, folding into NotifyCompleteMultipleDegraded, which deliberately names no specific family. A run degraded here therefore reached the operator as 'two or more families degraded, check the execution record'. This is the named surface. The Message deliberately does NOT name a cause: this Catch is reached by a fan-in COVERAGE BREACH (CostCoverageError), by 'unable to measure' (CostCoverageUnmeasured), by a capture-stream staleness raise (CostCaptureStaleError) and by an ordinary Lambda failure, and the state cannot tell them apart — all four are truthfully reported as 'the cost record for this cycle was not written'.

Parameters.Subject: Alpha Engine Weekly Pipeline — AggregateCosts WARNING (cost record for this cycle not written)
Parameters.Message: AggregateCosts (the weekly cost-telemetry aggregation, decision_artifacts/_cost/{run_date}/cost.parquet) failed — see $.aggregate_costs_error on the execution record for detail. Reached by an ordinary Lambda failure, by a fan-in COVERAGE BREACH (a stage ran and emitted no cost record, or an undeclared producer appeared), by the coverage check being unable to measure, or by a stale capture stream; the alert does not try to tell them apart because the operator consequence is the same. NON-FATAL for trading: no research, prediction, backtest or execution artifact depends on this parquet, and the run's own work is unaffected. It is NOT nothing: this cycle has no LLM cost attribution, AlphaEngine/Cost is missing a week, and a coverage breach means spend was attributed to nothing at all. The run therefore terminates DEGRADED. View pipeline status: https://dashboard.nousergon.ai/pipeline-status

Catch.Comment: Best-effort alert — a publish failure must not block the non-fatal path this alert decorates. $.degraded_summary and $.aggregate_costs_degraded are already set, so the run still terminates DEGRADED.

CheckShellRunNotify.Comment: Consolidated Friday-PM shell-run result notify. Reuses the EXISTING NotifyComplete SNS-publish substrate (same alpha-engine-alerts topic, same arn:aws:states:::sns:publish Resource) with a shell_run-tagged Subject/Message so the operator can tell a Friday dry-pass result apart from a real Saturday SUCCESS in their inbox. shell_run absent/false → NotifyComplete (BYTE-IDENTICAL to pre-spine). shell_run=true → NotifyShellRunComplete. No new SNS topic / Lambda / infra — the consolidated per-state pass/fail report (ROADMAP design point 5) is a scoped follow-on; the spine delivers a single shell-run-tagged success signal by reusing NotifyComplete's pattern.

CheckGateDegradedNotify.Comment: config#2278 + config#2276 + config#6685 + alpha-engine-config-I6025 + alpha-engine-config#6722: a green run that could not run its pre-spend gates (gate_degraded — set by the LibPinGateDegraded / PipelineContractGateDegraded / SetMutexAcquireDegradedFlag Pass states), and/or its tail health checks (health_check_degraded — set ONLY by the SaturdayHealthCheckDegraded / SubstrateHealthCheckDegraded Pass states), and/or ReportCard's advisory grading (report_card_degraded — set ONLY by ReportCardDegraded, config#6685), and/or the Parity verdict (parity_degraded — set ONLY by ParityDegraded, alpha-engine-config-I6025/I6044: absence of a parity verdict must never render as a clean pass), and/or ResearchPredictorParallel's own internal fail-open Catch routes (research_predictor_degraded — set ONLY by SetResearchPredictorDegraded, alpha-engine-config#6722) must SAY SO in the completion email (weekly-sf-policy.md §2.3 / §2.3a). All five are SF-controlled booleans, IsPresent-guarded per config#2275. Rules are ordered most-specific-first: research_predictor_degraded ALWAYS routes to the generic NotifyCompleteMultipleDegraded first, regardless of any other flag — deliberately given NO single-flag notifier of its own (unlike the other four) because it already covers 25+ distinct internal fail-open routes; adding a sixth per-combination axis on top would multiply the enumeration this Choice already avoids for the fourth flag (parity_degraded, next). parity_degraded combined with ANY other family also routes to NotifyCompleteMultipleDegraded (mirrors the report_card_degraded fold below — the config#2276 comment's predicted 'third flag family' generalizes further the same way: fold into the existing generic combined notifier rather than enumerating more per-combination hardcoded Task states); then report_card_degraded combined with EITHER remaining family also routes to NotifyCompleteMultipleDegraded (config#6685); the pre-existing gates+health / gates-only / health-only rules are UNCHANGED (each still implies report_card_degraded, parity_degraded and research_predictor_degraded are all absent, since any of those being true is intercepted by the rules ahead of them); report_card_degraded alone gets its own single-flag notifier (NotifyCompleteReportCardDegraded) mirroring NotifyCompleteGatesDegraded/NotifyCompleteHealthDegraded exactly, and parity_degraded alone (all three other flags absent) gets NotifyCompleteParityDegraded (alpha-engine-config-I6025), same shape. Each still routes to a SEPARATE hardcoded-constant notifier rather than States.Format-ing flags into NotifyComplete — preserving config#1819's Subject/Message-are-constants invariant. Name retained from config#2278 (it is the wave-1 chain anchor referenced across tests/comments) — read it as the degraded-completion selector.

Choices.Comment: alpha-engine-config-I7813. LAST in the list on purpose: a run that also degraded a gate, a health check, the parity verdict, the report card or a Branch A fail-open matches one of the rules above and gets that (more consequential) notification, while the leaf's own PublishScannerLeaderboardDegraded alert has already named it. This rule exists so a run whose ONLY degradation is the observe-only board cannot reach NotifyComplete's "All steps completed successfully" while terminating in DegradedRun.

alpha-engine-config-I7194. The sixth flag family, and the second one folded into the generic combined notifier rather than given a per-combination Task of its own — the generalization config#2276's comment predicted and config#6722 already applied to research_predictor_degraded. LAST in the list on purpose, for the same reason the scanner-leaderboard rule above it is: a run that also degraded a gate, a health check, the parity verdict, the report card, the leaf or a Branch A fail-open matches one of the rules above and gets that (more consequential) notification. This rule exists so a run whose ONLY degradation is the cost aggregation cannot reach NotifyComplete's "All steps completed successfully" while terminating in DegradedRun — which is what it would have done from the top level, where the branch-local $.research_degraded_local hoist that used to carry it does not reach.

One of exactly TWO legal writers of $.parity_degraded (the other: ParityCompareDegraded) — pinned by tests/test_sf_parity_degraded_wiring.py. weekly-sf-policy §2.3 honest-degradation: the run CONTINUES — to the PitParityCompare join (which emits verdict UNKNOWN for missing pass artifacts, §2.3a), then Evaluator/ReportCard/Director.

The compare will emit the parity verdict as UNKNOWN for any missing pass artifact — absence of a verdict must NOT be read as a clean pass (sf-pipeline-policy §2.3a). Which branch: $.parity_branch_outcomes on the execution record (per-branch specifics at $.pit_parity_lookahead_poll / $.pit_parity_walkforward_poll / $.parity_replay_poll and *_error). Rerun ONLY the failed branch via scripts/weekly_sf_rerun.py --dry-run (it derives skip flags for the completed branches). View pipeline status: https://dashboard.nousergon.ai/pipeline-status

NormalizeFailureContext.Comment: config#1819 notifier-totality fix. Single Catch/Next target for EVERY failure path before HandleFailure — structurally guarantees the fields HandleFailure's States.Format/JsonToString template consumes ($.error, $.pipeline_label, $.sns_topic_arn) are present, regardless of what any upstream Catch, Extract*Error normalizer, or manual Execution.Input supplied. Mirrors the InitializeInput JsonMerge-defaults idiom (defaults as the base/first-arg, current state $ as the override/second-arg — second-arg wins — so a real $.error from a Catch's ResultPath always survives). 2026-07-02 incident (offcycle-shell-20260703-005835): a manual-trigger input omitted pipeline_label and HandleFailure's States.Format('Saturday{} Pipeline failed...', $.pipeline_label, ...) threw States.Runtime, masking the true underlying error — this state closes that CLASS (not just this instance). error/sns_topic_arn get a floor default here for defense-in-depth against any FUTURE Catch that forgets its own ResultPath: $.error (every CURRENT path already sets $.error via a Task Catch ResultPath or an Extract*Error Pass, so this is a backstop, not a behavior change for today's paths). pipeline_label is ALSO re-pinned by NormalizeFailureContextRepin (next state) from $.shell_run rather than trusted verbatim — closes the Subject-injection shape (an arbitrary/oversized/newline-bearing manual pipeline_label reaching HandleFailure's States.Format Subject; SNS Subject must be <=100 chars with no newlines) at the root, the same class of bug as the 2026-06-12 NotifyComplete Subject crash (SNS.InvalidParameterException). PROVENANCE (config#2281): the sns_topic_arn literal in this JsonMerge is the failure-path FLOOR of last resort — the merge keeps any already-present $.sns_topic_arn (the execution-input-sourced value from InitializeInput); the literal engages only if the input context was lost upstream. Kept in lockstep with InitializeInput's floor by tests/test_sf_sns_arn_single_source.py.

NormalizeFailureContextRepin.Comment: Re-derive $.pipeline_label from $.shell_run (a boolean the SF itself controls) instead of trusting whatever string a manual Execution.Input supplied for pipeline_label — closes the SNS Subject-injection vector at HandleFailure's States.Format('Alpha Engine Saturday{} Pipeline — FAILED', $.pipeline_label): an arbitrary/oversized/newline-bearing manual pipeline_label can no longer reach the Subject regardless of what NormalizeFailureContext's floor-default merge left in place. IsPresent guards make this Choice total — it cannot itself raise a missing-$.shell_run States.Runtime, unlike a bare States.Format/JsonToString would. shell_run=true -> ' Preflight' (matches ApplyShellRunDefaults' identity so a Friday shell-run failure still reads 'Saturday Preflight Pipeline — FAILED'); anything else (absent, false, or a non-boolean) -> '' (the real Saturday identity).

NormalizeFailureContextPreflightLabel.Comment: shell_run=true path: pin pipeline_label to ' Preflight' (leading space, same convention as ApplyShellRunDefaults/preflight_args) so a Friday shell-run failure still surfaces 'Saturday Preflight Pipeline — FAILED', matching the pre-fix labeling behavior exactly.

NormalizeFailureContextRealLabel.Comment: shell_run absent/false/non-boolean path (the real Saturday run, and any other cadence): pin pipeline_label to '' so HandleFailure surfaces the byte-identical pre-fix 'Alpha Engine Saturday Pipeline — FAILED' Subject. This OVERRIDES whatever pipeline_label value (if any) a manual Execution.Input or upstream state left in place — the label is now always SF-derived, never free-text passthrough, closing the Subject-injection vector structurally rather than by string-truncation (ASL has no substring/truncate intrinsic).

HandleFailure.Comment: Failure alert via SNS — pipeline halts. Subject + Message are parameterized via States.Format on $.pipeline_label so a Preflight Pipeline failure surfaces 'Saturday Preflight Pipeline — FAILED' (shell_run=true → ApplyShellRunDefaults sets $.pipeline_label=' Preflight') while a real Saturday SF failure surfaces 'Saturday Pipeline — FAILED' ($.pipeline_label='' from InitializeInput defaults). 2026-05-23 rename arc: 'shell_run' is internal mechanism-language; alerts surface the user-facing 'Preflight' label. config#1819 (2026-07-06): every path into this state now routes through NormalizeFailureContext -> NormalizeFailureContextRepin first (the ONLY Catch/Next target for the whole failure path), which structurally guarantees $.error/$.sns_topic_arn/$.pipeline_label are present AND re-pins pipeline_label from $.shell_run rather than trusting a manual Execution.Input's free-text value — so this Subject can never exceed the SNS 100-char/no-newline contract and this States.Format can never throw States.Runtime for a missing JSONPath, closing both the 2026-07-02 States.Runtime-masking incident and the Subject-injection shape of the 2026-06-12 NotifyComplete crash.

Parameters.Message.$: States.Format('Saturday{} Pipeline failed. Error: {}. View the failing state + per-state detail at https://dashboard.nousergon.ai/pipeline-status  (redrive-execution is a no-op on this pipeline: every Task Catch routes to this shared FailExecution state, so redrive just re-enters FailExecution and re-fails immediately with no retry. To retry MECHANICALLY: from a nousergon-data checkout run  python3 scripts/weekly_sf_rerun.py --dry-run  -- it derives the original run_date + the correct skip_* set from this failed execution and handles the run-slot mutex; review, then rerun with --start. Manual fallback: start a fresh execution with skip_* input flags set true for stages already completed, e.g. skip_morning_enrich / skip_data_phase1 / skip_backtester -- see infrastructure/README.md for the full flag list and rationale.)', $.pipeline_label, States.JsonToString($.error))

FailExecution.Comment: config#5601 — the terminal Fail carries the UNDERLYING error, not a constant. Before this, EVERY failure of this pipeline terminated with the identical static Cause, so states:DescribeExecution reported 41 of the last 60 runs as the same opaque 'PipelineFailure' and no control-plane consumer — dashboard, console, or any failure histogram — could tell one failure mode from another. The information already existed and was already correct: NormalizeFailureContext (config#1819) guarantees $.error is present, and HandleFailure renders it into the SNS body with this exact expression. It simply never reached the EXECUTION RECORD, so 'is this one bug recurring or forty different bugs' could only be answered by opening CloudWatch per run, by hand. That is what kept the daily exercise cadence (config#5489) from converging: 5x the attempts, but every attempt still ended in a manual archaeology dig. | SAFETY: CausePath is evaluated at runtime and throws States.Runtime on a missing path, which would REPLACE the real failure with a runtime error — the worst regression available here. It is safe because this state has exactly ONE inbound edge (HandleFailure), and all 30 failure paths reach HandleFailure through NormalizeFailureContext, whose entire purpose is to guarantee $.error. States.JsonToString($.error) is the SAME expression HandleFailure's Message parameter already runs in production. | Error stays the static 'PipelineFailure' literal deliberately: consumers key on it, and per-run detail belongs in Cause.
FailExecution.CausePath: States.Format('Pipeline step failed: {}. Do NOT redrive-execution: every Task Catch in this pipeline routes to this shared FailExecution state, so redrive is a deterministic no-op (it re-enters FailExecution and re-fails immediately with the same stale input). To retry MECHANICALLY: from a nousergon-data checkout run  python3 scripts/weekly_sf_rerun.py --dry-run  -- it derives the original run_date + the correct skip_* set from this failed execution and handles the run-slot mutex; review, then rerun with --start. SubstrateHealthGate.Comment: config#2249: fast pre-dispatch substrate health gate, immediately before MorningEnrich (the first state to actually dispatch work to the Saturday box). A dead/unhealthy dispatch box (disk full, or the SSM agent wedged/unresponsive so a command silently never registers) used to be discovered only after MorningEnrich burned its full 'gold 4+2' retry ladder (config#2279, up to ~15 min) before falling into the generic PipelineFailure path. This ONE Lambda invocation issues its own tiny SSM `df` probe command and polls it to a terminal status internally (bounded well under this Task's own TimeoutSeconds), returning verdict=HEALTHY or verdict=SUBSTRATE_UNHEALTHY with a distinct reason (disk_full / ssm_unresponsive / ssm_command_never_registered) — see infrastructure/lambdas/substrate-health-gate/index.py. Deliberately a SEPARATE fast pre-check, not a replacement for MorningEnrich's own resilience: MorningEnrich keeps its full retry ladder for real transient issues once dispatch is confirmed healthy. Adds ~10-20s to every Saturday run (accepted — the Saturday run has slack, unlike the tight weekday pre-open buffer; NOT wired into the weekday SF). ResultSelector captures the WHOLE Lambda payload under .gate (verdict/message/reason/disk_used_percent/...) rather than cherry-picking $.Payload.<key>: the Lambda's documented contract emits `reason` ONLY on the SUBSTRATE_UNHEALTHY verdicts, so a prior per-key select of `reason.$: $.Payload.reason` crashed EVERY healthy run with States.Runtime '$.Payload.reason could not be found' (the gate could never pass on a healthy box — surfaced by the 2026-07-17 Friday preflight shell run). Passthrough lets each consumer read only fields the producer guarantees for its branch (Choice reads .gate.verdict; the non-HEALTHY Extract reads .gate.reason). Contract regression-guarded by tests/test_sf_substrate_gate_contract_wiring.py. | alpha-engine-config-I8809: PARTITION FAMILY = trading_day - $.run_date is the cycle's trading day from NormalizeRunDates. It keys no artifact here (this gate declares output: none) — its only use is the stage-coverage assertion's grouping key (alpha-engine-config-I10172), and it must be the trading day because that is what every other Lambda-backed coverage-asserting state in this graph keys its verdict by.

CheckSubstrateHealthGate.Comment: config#2249: branches on SubstrateHealthGate's verdict. HEALTHY -> proceed into MorningEnrich as normal. SUBSTRATE_UNHEALTHY (any reason) -> short-circuit straight to the named-failure path WITHOUT ever entering MorningEnrich's own retry ladder — the whole point is failing fast (<2 min) instead of burning ~15 min discovering the same dead box via 4 retries.

CheckSpotDispatchNeeded.Comment: config#2248 (root-cause fix for the always-on dashboard box SPOF): the 14 downstream sendCommand/Lambda states (MorningEnrich through WeeklySubstrateHealthCheck, plus SubstrateHealthGate's Payload) all key off $.ec2_instance_id. That field is no longer a hardcoded literal in the SaturdayTrigger EventBridge Input or the Friday shell-run trigger Lambda (both stripped by config#2248) — it is populated HERE, either by an already-present operator/rerun value (this Choice's first branch: scripts/weekly_sf_rerun.py's rerun_input() passes the ORIGINAL failed execution's ec2_instance_id through verbatim, so a watch-rerun reuses the same still-live launcher box instead of paying for a second spot launch) or by a fresh ephemeral spot this Choice's Default branch dispatches via DispatchWeeklyFreshnessSpot. Sits where CheckMutexRole's cadence-acquire path (via AcquireMutex) AND its bypass Default (operator/recovery/non-cadence roles, which skip the mutex entirely) BOTH converge -- so every execution passes through this gate exactly once, regardless of pipeline_role, never burning a spot launch on a mutex conflict -- and BEFORE CheckShellRun / any of the 14 consumer states (nothing may reference $.ec2_instance_id before this gate resolves it). alpha-engine-config-I8162 adds the SECOND branch: bypass the dispatch entirely when EVERY stage that SSM-invokes onto $.ec2_instance_id is skipped by this execution's input, landing straight on the same CheckShellRun convergence with no ec2_instance_id at all (nothing downstream dereferences it once all of those stages are gated off). The conjunction is NOT hand-maintained here: it is DERIVED from scripts/weekly_sf_rerun.py's STAGES table by reachability over this definition (box_dispatch_flags) and pinned to this state by tests/test_weekly_sf_rerun.py::TestSpotDispatchOnlyWhenABoxStageSurvives. Parameters.Subject: Alpha Engine Weekly Pipeline — ScannerLeaderboard WARNING (observe-only board not written)
Parameters.Message: ScannerLeaderboard (the observe-only scanner champion/challenger board, scanner/leaderboard/{run_date}.json) failed — see $.scanner_leaderboard_error on the execution record for detail. NON-FATAL for trading: nothing branches on this board, and the week's signals, predictions, report card and Director advisory are unaffected. It is NOT nothing: the scanner champion/challenger comparison has no observation for this cycle, and the run therefore terminates DEGRADED. View pipeline status: https://dashboard.nousergon.ai/pipeline-status

Catch.Comment: Best-effort alert — a publish failure must not block the non-fatal path this alert decorates. $.degraded_summary is already set, so the run still terminates DEGRADED.

NotifyCompleteScannerLeaderboardDegraded.Comment: alpha-engine-config-I7813: terminal notification for a run whose ONLY degradation is the observe-only board. Registered LAST in CheckGateDegradedNotify's choice list, immediately before the clean Default — so any run that also degraded a gate, a health check, the parity verdict, the report card or a Branch A fail-open still gets that stage's (or the multi-) notification, which is the more consequential fact. This state exists so the leaf can never reach NotifyComplete's "All steps completed successfully" while terminating in DegradedRun.

Parameters.Subject: Alpha Engine Saturday Pipeline — DEGRADED: scanner leaderboard (run terminates FAILED)
Parameters.Message: Every WORK stage completed, and the run still terminates FAILED (config-I6891, sf-pipeline-policy.md §2.3 Option A) because the ScannerLeaderboard leaf failed and scanner/leaderboard/{run_date}.json was not written; a scanner-leaderboard-degraded alert fired earlier in this run. See $.scanner_leaderboard_error on the execution record for detail. The week's trading artifacts, report card and Director advisory are unaffected — no stage branches on this board — but the scanner champion/challenger comparison has no observation for this cycle. View pipeline status: https://dashboard.nousergon.ai/pipeline-status

Catch.Comment: config#1819 — best-effort: a terminal notifier must never change the outcome it reports. The run still routes to CheckDegradedOutcome and terminates DEGRADED.

DirectorComplete.Comment: config#6054: success-only witness for the rerun deriver (scripts/weekly_sf_rerun.py). Director's success and every bypass path previously converged on CheckShellRunNotify, so no state uniquely witnessed 'Director actually completed' — the I6055-class trap: a rerun could mark a bypassed Director complete and skip it. Entered ONLY via Director's success edge.

BacktesterLivenessGate.Comment: config#6938: liveness branch. StatusDetails Undeliverable/Terminated means the launcher box is GONE (a spot reclaim, the failure mode most expected on this substrate), not that Backtester failed. Without this the two are indistinguishable in the alert and the run dies as a Backtester fault — measured on watch-rerun-2026-08-10-8 (2026-08-11): ResponseCode -1 / Undeliverable, no log shipped, Server.SpotInstanceTermination on neighbouring instances in the same window. Fail fast with a distinguishable phase rather than re-issuing: this sendCommand targets $.ec2_instance_id, the SHARED launcher from DispatchWeeklyFreshnessSpot, so when it is reclaimed every remaining stage is equally dead and a per-stage rebind would fix one symptom of a pipeline-wide loss. Mirrors config#5688's four gates; recovery is the mechanical scripts/weekly_sf_rerun.py.

ExtractBacktesterSubstrateLostError.Comment: config#6938: the SUBSTRATE-LOST sibling of ExtractBacktesterError. Same normalization, distinguishable phase, same downstream hand-off — so an operator can tell a reclaimed box from a Backtester failure without opening the execution history.

CheckDegradedOutcome.Comment: Option-A parity for the weekly pipeline (alpha-engine-config-I6891). The 2026-07-28 Option-A ruling (alpha-engine-config#2699) reached both weekday definitions (#6692, #6722) and never reached this one: every degraded weekly run terminated SUCCEEDED and wrote a completion marker claiming status SUCCEEDED, so a run that did not really work counted as one that did. sf-pipeline-policy.md 2.3: a degraded run writes status DEGRADED and ends in a Fail state so status-keyed watchers engage. This is the single chokepoint every real-completion path now passes through, so a fail-open route added later inherits the honest terminal by writing $.degraded_summary and touching nothing here. $.degraded_summary is only assigned on a degraded path — a fully green run never sets it — so the IsPresent guard is load-bearing: an unguarded dereference throws States.Runtime at the last state of an otherwise successful weekly run (the config-I2767 shape, mirrored from step_function_daily.json's CheckDegradedOutcome). Absent flag = never degraded = WriteCompletionMarker via Default, which is the semantically exact reading.

CheckShellRunDegradedOutcome.Comment: alpha-engine-config-I6891: the Friday-PM preflight twin of CheckDegradedOutcome. The shell-run branch leaves CheckShellRunNotify BEFORE CheckGateDegradedNotify, so a preflight run whose gates, health checks, parity verdict or report card degraded previously ended SUCCEEDED with no honest terminal at all — the same defect as the real-run path, on the path that exists to prove the real run will work. Same IsPresent guard, same DegradedRun terminal; neither edge writes a completion marker, because a preflight dry-pass is not a weekly completion (see WriteCompletionMarker).

ShellRunComplete.Comment: alpha-engine-config-I6891: the clean Friday-PM preflight terminal. Byte-equivalent in outcome to the End: true NotifyShellRunComplete previously carried — a green preflight still ends SUCCEEDED and still writes no completion marker; only the degraded edge changed.

WeeklyCoverageSweep.Comment: WeeklyCoverageSweep (alpha-engine-config-I8214, carrying I8154 deliverable 4 and I8186's state-machine half) — runs nousergon_lib's stage-coverage sweep over THIS cycle and augments the completion marker the previous state just wrote with the cycle's real shape. WHY IT EXISTS: the sweep's READER shipped in nousergon-lib and nothing called it, so it detected nothing. This state is its caller. PLACEMENT: immediately after WriteCompletionMarker, deliberately — the marker must exist before it can be augmented. The marker the SF writes claims only 'this SF execution reached its terminal' (claim: sf_execution_terminal, cycle_verdict: unknown); this state is what upgrades that to a cycle verdict. On 2026-08-22 the marker was written by an execution that entered 1 of 16 declared stages and said nothing about it. WHY A LAMBDA AND NOT AN SSM COMMAND: this pipeline has no always-on box — $.ec2_instance_id is an ephemeral spot, and since alpha-engine-config-I8162 a recovery run whose every box stage is skipped carries NO instance id at all, which is exactly the run that most needs a coverage verdict. A sweep dereferencing it would throw States.Runtime one state after the pipeline's own success terminal. Mirrors weekly-run-scope, the sibling Lambda that reads the same execution history for the same pipeline. OBSERVE-ONLY TAIL, a design constraint not an omission: everything from here down is downstream of the real success terminal and must never turn a completed weekly run into a failure (sf-pipeline-policy §2.1 blast radius). Every terminal below is a Succeed, and the Catch routes to the unobserved terminal rather than to a failure. THREE OUTCOMES AND 'DID NOT RUN' IS NOT ONE OF THE OTHER TWO: the handler returns outcome clean / findings / unavailable. Findings have ALREADY paged from inside the handler (krepis.alerts, deduped per pipeline+run_date), so nothing pages again here; 'unavailable' is the one case the sweep cannot page for itself, so the state machine does it. Collapsing unavailable into findings renders an unobserved surface as a detection, and collapsing it into clean renders it green (principles.md §2.7). PREFLIGHT-AWARE: dry_run.$ = $.research_dry — the Friday-PM shell run exercises the whole read path and every IAM grant, and writes nothing. TIMEOUT: 240s, deliberately BELOW the Lambda's own 300s so the SF ceiling is the one that binds (tests/test_sf_lambda_timeout_ordering.py). MEASURED, not guessed: the first live invocation on 2026-08-22 took 29.4s at 1024 MB with a 675 MB peak, walking 40 executions of the cycle. The original 90s/120s/256MB sizing TIMED OUT at 120s — at 256 MB the function used 256 of 256 MB and Lambda scales CPU with memory, so it was throttled as well as starved. 240s is ~8x the measured runtime; the budget bounds an unbounded walk, it does not size the work. DEGRADED PATH DELIBERATELY NOT WIRED: WriteCompletionMarkerDegraded must keep flowing straight into DegradedRun (a Fail state) or sf-telegram-notifier's 'Error: DegradedRun' consumer contract breaks (alpha-engine-config-I6891). A degraded cycle's coverage is swept out-of-band instead. | alpha-engine-config-I8809: PARTITION FAMILY = trading_day, with calendar_date passed as the LEGACY family. The sweep unions both _stage_coverage partitions (canonical first; a verdict in the trading-day partition wins a duplicate) until the 2026-09-05 cutover, so this cycle reports against ONE logical cycle and pages no false absences. Its dry run on 2026-08-22 logged '9 covered / 1 findings / 28 absent of 39 expected' - the 28 were in the sibling partition. nousergon-lib read_coverage_sweep(calendar_date=...) is the reader half; the pin in infrastructure/lambdas/weekly-coverage-sweep/requirements.txt is what carries it. | alpha-engine-config-I10170 — THE OBSERVER. observer_execution_arn.$ = $$.Execution.Id. This state runs INSIDE the execution it grades, so that execution is RUNNING at the instant it grades, on every run, forever. Measured on the live 2026-09-04 cycle: the sweep at 21:39:18Z wrote cycle.verdict in_flight / still_running and paged 13 stages absent in the SAME artifact, while watch-rerun-2026-09-04-4 - the execution it called RUNNING - stopped at 21:39:19Z, one second later, two hops past this state. The 2026-08-28 artifact carries the identical pair, so this was the mechanism's normal state and not an incident. Two consequences, and the second reaches other systems: (1) IN_FLIGHT could never mean what it says, so a cycle genuinely still running was indistinguishable from every healthy one; (2) augment_marker stamped cycle_verdict in_flight and did_work false onto the completion marker of a COMPLETED cycle - the object every gate:* Verified-when predicate reads, which is alpha-engine-config-I8186 re-created with the sign flipped. Naming the observer lets nousergon_lib count this execution's entered states (real work) without letting its status make its own cycle non-terminal; ANY OTHER running execution still yields in_flight, so the honest 'not yet gradeable' answer survives for the case that means it. A FOURTH OUTCOME: 'deferred' - the sweep ran and the cycle could not support the absence claim, so the absent count is WITHHELD rather than asserted. Its own Choice branch and terminal below; collapsing it into 'clean' renders an unestablished surface green and collapsing it into 'findings' reports an assertion the sweep just declined to make. | alpha-engine-config-I9693: this state's payload now also carries `observer_did_work` — whether THIS execution entered any declared spine stage — which `CheckExecutionDidWork` (its new Next) reads. No new call, no new grant: the sweep already computed the per-execution breakdown to build the cycle.

Catch.Comment: A sweep that could not be INVOKED is the did-not-run case, and it is the one case the handler cannot report for itself because it never started. Routes to the unobserved terminal, which pages — never to the clean one.

CheckExecutionDidWork.Comment: alpha-engine-config-I9693 - THE VACUOUS-RUN TERMINAL. An execution that entered NONE of the pipeline's declared spine stages must not reach a Succeed terminal. MEASURED, five consecutive Saturdays: every scheduled weekly run 2026-08-15 through 2026-09-12 FAILED (five DIFFERENT causes - PredictorBacktest rc=1, a Director APITimeoutError, weekly_aggregate_costs_fail_open twice, and an SNS AuthorizationError in HandleFailure), and every one was 'recovered' by an operator rerun with every producer skipped, which reported SUCCEEDED. watch-rerun-2026-09-11-1 set 26 skip_* flags, entered ZERO of the 16 declared spine stages, ran 2m03s, and is indistinguishable from a four-hour full run in list-executions. A green recovery path is worse than a red run because it stops anyone looking (engagement-protocol-policy 5: detection blindness outranks the defects it hides). sf-pipeline-policy.md 2.3: a run that reaches its terminal having skipped its work must not terminate as a clean success - the same Option-A ruling (2026-07-28, alpha-engine-config#2699) that gave this definition its DegradedRun terminal, applied one level up, to a run that was not degraded because it never started. | WHY HERE AND NOT EARLIER: the completion marker and the coverage sweep both still run on a vacuous execution, and must - alpha-engine-config-I8186 explicitly forbids fixing this by making WriteCompletionMarker unreachable from recovery reruns, because a genuine recovery that DOES complete the spine has to keep writing it. The discriminator is the work verdict, never the execution's role or its name. This Choice is therefore the LAST thing the run does, after the marker is written and after the sweep has augmented it with the cycle's real shape. | WHY IT IS NOT A WIDENED SUCCESS CONDITION IN REVERSE: it fires ONLY on an explicit boolean false. Absent, null, or any non-boolean value takes the Default and the run terminates exactly as it did before - a sweep that could not read the cycle reports outcome=unavailable and pages through WeeklyCoverageSweepUnavailable, which is the surface for an unmeasured run. An unknown is never rendered green AND never manufactured into a red. | NOT REACHABLE FROM THE THU/FRI GATE-OUT (WeeklyRunDaySkip terminates upstream of every stage) NOR FROM THE FRIDAY-PM SHELL RUN (its only terminals are ShellRunComplete and DegradedRun; it never enters WriteCompletionMarker or this tail), so neither designed no-op can be turned red by this.

VacuousRun.Comment: alpha-engine-config-I9693. Error is a consumer contract, exactly as DegradedRun's is: sf-telegram-notifier keys its rendering off the literal, so a run that did no work reads as 'did no work' and not as a crash. The completion marker for this cycle HAS been written and HAS been augmented with the cycle's real shape by the time this is entered - nousergon_lib.pipeline_status.completion_marker.marker_verdict is the field to read for the CYCLE's verdict; this terminal is the statement about THIS EXECUTION, and it is the one list-executions can see. | alpha-engine-config-I8809: PARTITION FAMILY = trading_day. $.run_date is the cycle's trading day from NormalizeRunDates, and this cause names WHICH CYCLE this execution contributed nothing to — not when it fired.
VacuousRun.CausePath: States.Format('Weekly freshness pipeline VACUOUS RUN - this execution entered none of the declared spine stages and dispatched no work, so it must not report SUCCEEDED (alpha-engine-config-I9693). Run date: {}. Sweep explanation: {}. Observer detail: {}. This is NOT a pipeline failure: the completion marker for this cycle was written and carries the cycle verdict under cycle / cycle_verdict - read those, not this execution status, to learn whether the WEEK work happened. What this terminal asserts is narrower and was previously unsayable: THIS execution did none of it. If this fired on a rerun you intended to be narrow, the rerun was narrower than you intended - scripts/weekly_sf_rerun.py derives a coherent skip-set from the failed execution history rather than skipping everything.', $.run_date, $.coverage_sweep.payload.explanation, States.JsonToString($.coverage_sweep.payload.observer))

CheckWeeklyCoverageSweepOutcome.Comment: The handler's outcome IS the verdict; each value gets its own named terminal so the execution history says which happened. $.coverage_sweep.outcome is now IsPresent-guarded rather than relying on a flooring proof (alpha-engine-config-I9693): the sole predecessor USED to be WeeklyCoverageSweep, which pins it via ResultSelector (config#2275 rule 3b), and is now CheckExecutionDidWork, a Choice that pins nothing. The guard makes the safety local instead of inherited - an absent outcome lands on the Default, which is the UNAVAILABLE terminal, so the behaviour is unchanged and only the proof moved. The Default is the UNOBSERVED terminal, not the clean one — an outcome this Choice does not recognise is an unknown state of the coverage surface, and unknown is never rendered green. | alpha-engine-config-I10170: 'deferred' is the fourth outcome and has its own branch. It is NOT unavailable (the sweep ran) and NOT clean (coverage was not established).

WeeklyCoverageSweepClean.Comment: outcome=clean: the sweep ran and found no coverage gap. The marker WriteCompletionMarker wrote a moment earlier now carries the cycle's real shape, so its cycle_verdict is no longer 'unknown'.

WeeklyCoverageSweepFindings.Comment: outcome=findings: the sweep ran and found a gap. It has ALREADY paged from inside the handler (krepis.alerts, dedup_key stage-coverage-sweep/<pipeline>/<run_date>) — no second publish here, which would render one finding as two incidents. Succeed rather than Fail because the weekly run itself completed: this terminal reports on the SWEEP, and failing the execution would retroactively mark a good run bad, which is the misattribution alpha-engine-config-I8045 is about.

WeeklyCoverageSweepUnavailable.Comment: outcome=unavailable, an unrecognised outcome, or an invoke failure: the sweep DID NOT RUN, or ran and could not publish what it found. This is the branch that must page from the state machine, because a handler that never started cannot page for itself, and 'found nothing' and 'did not run' are different facts (principles.md §2.7). Fail-open to Succeed after publishing: the weekly run completed and its completion is not in question — what is unobserved is the coverage check over it. | alpha-engine-config-I8809: PARTITION FAMILY = trading_day (pass-through). This state does not KEY on the date; it carries $.run_date into a summary payload or a notification body. It is named here anyway because the contract test requires every state touching a run-date variable to state which family it means — an undeclared site is how the split reappeared once already.

Parameters.Subject: Alpha Engine Weekly Pipeline - stage-coverage sweep DID NOT RUN
Parameters.Message.$: States.Format('The weekly run for {} completed and wrote its completion marker, but the stage-coverage sweep did not run, or ran and could not publish its result. The marker therefore keeps its bare envelope claim - cycle_verdict unknown - and no coverage verdict exists for this cycle. This is an UNOBSERVED surface, not a clean result. Re-run it by invoking the alpha-engine-weekly-coverage-sweep Lambda with run_date {} and state_machine_arn arn:aws:states:us-east-1:711398986525:stateMachine:ne-weekly-freshness-pipeline.', $.run_date, $.run_date)

Catch.Comment: config#1819 notifier convention: a failed notify must not fail the run.

WeeklyCoverageSweepUnobserved.Comment: Terminal for the did-not-run case, named for what is true — the coverage surface is unobserved for this cycle — rather than for the run, which completed.

WeeklyCoverageSweepDeferred.Comment: outcome=deferred (alpha-engine-config-I10170): the sweep RAN and declined to assert an absence its own cycle cannot support - the cycle is still IN_FLIGHT, or its ListExecutions contributor walk was truncated on a non-COMPLETED verdict, and under either condition a stage that has not finished is indistinguishable from one that finished and recorded nothing. WHY THIS PAGES: withholding is not silence. nousergon_lib withholds the StageCoverageSweepAbsent datapoint (publishing 0 would render an unestablished surface green - principles.md 2.7) and publishes StageCoverageSweepDeferred=1 in its place, so the deferral has its own datapoint rather than being inferred from another metric's silence; alpha-engine-stage-coverage-deferred alarms on it. The sweep has ALSO already paged from inside the handler on the coverage_deferred alert condition, which names every would-be-absent stage and the re-sweep command - this state's notification is the state-machine-visible record of the same fact, and both are deduped by krepis.alerts per pipeline+run_date. Succeed rather than Fail: the weekly run completed, and failing the execution would retroactively mark a good run bad (alpha-engine-config-I8045). | alpha-engine-config-I8809: PARTITION FAMILY = trading_day (pass-through). This state does not KEY on the date; it carries $.run_date into a notification body. Named here anyway because the contract test requires every state touching a run-date variable to state which family it means - an undeclared site is how the split reappeared once already.

Parameters.Subject: Alpha Engine Weekly Pipeline - stage-coverage sweep DEFERRED
Parameters.Message.$: States.Format('The weekly run for {} completed, and the stage-coverage sweep ran but could not establish coverage: the cycle was not terminal, or its contributor walk was truncated on a non-COMPLETED verdict. The absent count is WITHHELD, not zero - this is an UNESTABLISHED surface, not a clean result. Read s3://alpha-engine-research/_stage_coverage/_sweep/ne-weekly-freshness-pipeline/{}.json - its deferral_reason names the condition and absent_stages names every stage that had no verdict at sweep time. Re-sweep once the cycle is terminal by invoking the alpha-engine-weekly-coverage-sweep Lambda with run_date {} and state_machine_arn arn:aws:states:us-east-1:711398986525:stateMachine:ne-weekly-freshness-pipeline (omit observer_execution_arn - an out-of-band re-sweep observes from outside the cycle).', $.run_date, $.run_date, $.run_date)

Catch.Comment: config#1819 notifier convention: a failed notify must not fail the run.

WeeklyCoverageSweepUnestablished.Comment: The coverage of this cycle is UNESTABLISHED - the sweep ran, declined to assert an absence the cycle could not support, and said so (alpha-engine-config-I10170). Named separately from WeeklyCoverageSweepClean and WeeklyCoverageSweepUnobserved so the execution history says which of the three happened; a terminal shared with 'clean' would make the distinction unreadable in exactly the place an operator looks first.

WriteCompletionMarkerDegraded.Comment: alpha-engine-config-I6891, the DEGRADED twin of WriteCompletionMarker (shape mirrored from step_function_daily.json per the shared-code rule). Writes the SAME key as the clean marker with status DEGRADED and the full $.degraded_summary embedded, so a marker reader (pipeline-watchdog, sf-telegram-notifier, weekly_sf_recovery_metric) can tell a run that really worked from one that only ended. Deliberately EXCLUDES the Friday-PM preflight paths for the same reason WriteCompletionMarker does. No swallow-all Catch, same as the clean twin: a marker that cannot be written means this execution's own completion is unverifiable, which is the ambiguity the feature exists to surface rather than mask. ResultPath is LOAD-BEARING, not hygiene (alpha-engine-config-I6891): a Task with no ResultPath defaults to $, so the putObject result REPLACES the whole state input and the DegradedRun terminal's CausePath dereference of $.degraded_summary.reason cannot resolve. The execution then fails with States.Runtime instead of DegradedRun — and Error: DegradedRun is a consumer contract: sf-telegram-notifier's _is_degraded_run() keys its DEGRADED rendering off exactly that string, so every honestly-degraded run rendered as an ordinary crash-red FAILED with a truncated cause. Shipped in both weekday definitions since config#6692/#6722; the weekly one inherited it by mirroring them and it is fixed in all three here. | alpha-engine-config-I8809: PARTITION FAMILY = trading_day. $.run_date is the cycle's trading day from NormalizeRunDates, so this key names the CYCLE. Dual-written to the legacy calendar partition by the sibling state below until the 2026-09-05 cutover, per Brian's 2026-08-27 ruling - no history rewrite, and every consumer still reading the calendar family keeps working for one cycle.

Retry.Comment: Transient S3 fault coverage — mirrors the SendCommand SDK-transient Retry convention used elsewhere in this SF.

DegradedRun.CausePath: States.Format('Weekly freshness pipeline DEGRADED — reason: {}. Full degraded_summary: {}. Per the 2026-07-28 Option-A ruling (alpha-engine-config#2699), ported to this weekly SF via alpha-engine-config-I6891: a degraded run must FAIL so status-keyed watchers (sf-watch, EventBridge, sf-telegram-notifier) engage with zero new plumbing, and so a run that did not really work stops counting as one that did. The run was never aborted mid-pipeline — every fail-open continuation is unchanged; only the honesty of the terminal changes.', $.degraded_summary.reason, States.JsonToString($.degraded_summary))

RouteAfterBootstrapSuccess.Comment: A bootstrapped launcher box means one of two things. First boot: fall through to CheckShellRun and run the pipeline from stage 1. REPLACEMENT box after a substrate loss: resume at the interrupted stage instead -- falling through would re-run every stage the lost box already completed, which for the weekly pipeline means duplicate side effects (config#2252: duplicate model-zoo promotion emails) on top of hours of wasted compute.

SubstrateRelaunchGate.Comment: Substrate loss is an INFRASTRUCTURE event, not a workload failure: the ephemeral launcher spot was reclaimed (StatusDetails Undeliverable/Terminated) before the stage could report. Measured 2026-08-12: 3 of 11 recent spot requests in this account died instance-terminated-no-capacity, and one of them killed that day's scheduled weekly run mid-DataPhase1 (resource ids in config-I7119). Failing the execution here made every such reclaim a MANUAL recovery via scripts/weekly_sf_rerun.py -- detected-and-paged, which principles.md #3 counts as partial coverage, not automation. ONE bounded relaunch, forced ON-DEMAND: an on-demand box cannot be reclaimed, so a second substrate loss in the same execution is a genuine anomaly and stays terminal (and stays recoverable by weekly_sf_rerun.py, which is unchanged). The counter is spent per EXECUTION, not per stage, so this can never loop.

SetSubstrateRelaunchExhaustedError.Comment: Overwrites $.error rather than passing the stage's own substrate-lost error through: by the time the budget is spent, the operator-relevant fact is that the run lost TWO launcher boxes, which is a capacity event, not a DataPhase1 event. Writing $.error here is also what keeps this path inside the guaranteed-$.error chokepoint HandleFailure's States.JsonToString($.error) depends on.

Parameters.detail: launcher spot lost again after a forced on-demand relaunch; recover with scripts/weekly_sf_rerun.py

RecordSubstrateRelaunchAttempt.Comment: Spend the attempt BEFORE launching. If the relaunch or its bootstrap is itself lost, the gate is already exhausted and the execution fails loud instead of relaunching forever.

RelaunchWeeklyFreshnessSpot.Comment: Replacement launcher box after substrate loss. Identical to DispatchWeeklyFreshnessSpot except (a) force_on_demand=true -- the dispatcher has accepted that flag since config#2248 with the comment 'reserved for a future bounded retry-on-relaunch ... no current caller sets it', and this is that caller; spot-first here would re-enter the same exhausted pool that just reclaimed the box -- and (b) TimeoutSeconds 540 rather than 600, so the SF budget is the SMALLER of the two ceilings and is therefore the one that actually fires (config-I6897: an SF lambda:invoke declares two timeouts and only the smaller binds; DispatchWeeklyFreshnessSpot's own 600-vs-600 race is grandfathered in that issue and is deliberately NOT reproduced here). 540s is ample: the dispatcher fires the SSM bootstrap ASYNCHRONOUSLY and returns without waiting for the multi-minute clone + venv build. | alpha-engine-config-I8809: PARTITION FAMILY = trading_day - $.run_date is the cycle's trading day from NormalizeRunDates, and every artifact prefix and stage-coverage verdict this state produces keys off it. Downstream normalization with krepis.dates.resolve_trading_day is idempotent, so this is a no-op for consumers that already normalized and a convergence for those that did not.

Retry.Comment: config#2248: the launcher-box launch itself (spot capacity rotation, SSM-online wait) can transiently fail the same way any other spot dispatch in this fleet does — one backed-off retry before falling into the fail-loud Catch below.

MergeRelaunchedSpotInstanceId.Comment: Shallow JsonMerge with the new object second: $.ec2_instance_id is REPLACED, not appended. Every downstream SSM state addresses $.ec2_instance_id, so the replacement box is picked up everywhere at once. Then re-enter the SHARED bootstrap poll loop (InitWeeklyFreshnessSpotBootstrapPollCount) rather than a duplicate one, so a second substrate loss during re-bootstrap is handled by the same WeeklyFreshnessSpotBootstrapLivenessGate that handles the first.

ResumeAfterSubstrateRelaunch.Comment: Re-enter the pipeline at the interrupted stage, keyed off the phase label the Extract*SubstrateLostError normalizer already writes to $.error.phase -- the same label that reaches the SNS body, so the recovery path and the failure telemetry cannot drift apart. Each target is the stage's Task state, whose Next is its Init*PollCount state, so the stage's poll counter resets naturally. Every rule IsPresent-guards the path before dereferencing it (config#2275). Default is fail-loud: an unrecognised phase means a stage gained a substrate-lost branch without gaining a resume target, and guessing would silently skip work.

SetSubstrateResumeUnknownPhaseError.Comment: A relaunched box with no resume target. Unreachable by construction (tests/test_sf_substrate_relaunch_wiring.py derives the phase set from the definition), so reaching it means the definition changed without the wiring test -- fail loud and name that, rather than falling through to a stage and silently skipping the work the lost box never did.

Parameters.detail: relaunched launcher box has no resume target for this $.error.phase; the stage gained a substrate-lost branch without a resume branch

RunScope.Comment: RunScope (alpha-engine-config-I7620) — derives THIS execution's own scope and writes backtest/{run_date}/run_scope.json: one row per gated stage, each DISABLED / ENABLED_COMPLETED / ENABLED_FAILED / NOT_REACHED, with the skip_* flag that decided it. WHY IT EXISTS: which stages a run actually dispatched has never been recorded anywhere a consumer could read, so the Director grades the week without knowing which producers were switched off. On 2026-08-14 it reported the DELIBERATE absence of pit_parity (skip_parity:true on the Saturday EventBridge target since 2026-08-13, a recorded ruling) as 'contamination UNKNOWN — the producer never ran this cycle' and withheld issue_filing + loop_verification on the strength of it. WHY DERIVED, NOT A REGISTRY: private-docs/ already carries thirteen registries; a fourteenth listing enabled stages would be a hand-kept COPY of a fact whose two authorities are this definition and this execution's history, and it would drift the first time a stage is added. One flag flip in the CFN preset therefore changes the pipeline, the artifact and the Director's purview together. PLACEMENT: immediately before CheckSkipReportCard, so every work stage is already in the history it reads; the three states after it (itself, ReportCard, Director) resolve from the execution input instead, and every row records which source decided it. NON-FATAL: its Catch routes to CheckSkipReportCard — an advisory scope artifact must never kill a run that produced real trading artifacts, and the handler's own fail-open path emits a scope whose every stage is NOT_REACHED, which grades NOTHING and so cannot be mistaken for a narrow-but-clean run. PREFLIGHT-AWARE: dry_run.$=$.research_dry — the Friday-PM shell run exercises the full describe+history+derive path and writes nothing. CONSUMER: crucible-evaluator reads this state's OUTPUT IN-BAND — the ReportCard Task's Payload carries run_scope.$=$.run_scope_result.Payload — and falls back to the S3 artifact (alpha-engine-config-I7392, corrected 2026-08-29; it previously read the artifact ONLY). WHY THE ORDER WAS INVERTED: the artifact is the one delivery path a REHEARSAL is forbidden to use. This Lambda returns the derived scope and skips its put_object when dry_run is true, so on every Friday shell run the correct answer (Parity: DISABLED, CheckSkipParity took its skip branch) was derived, returned, and discarded on the way to its only consumer, and the card's contamination half resolved to UNKNOWN instead of NOT_IN_SCOPE. NormalizeRunDates.Comment: NormalizeRunDates (alpha-engine-config-I8809) - ONE normalization, at the graph's entry. Overwrites $.run_date with the cycle's TRADING day and stamps run_date_family='trading_day'. Every downstream consumer that already normalizes for itself (crucible-backtester/infrastructure/_spot_common.sh, crucible-research's signals_envelope and ChallengerShadow handlers, the evaluator and Director) becomes a NO-OP, because krepis.dates.resolve_trading_day is IDEMPOTENT BY CONTRACT - a trading-day input returns unchanged. Every consumer that used $.run_date RAW converges onto the same partition. That is the whole fix: the split existed because normalization was per-consumer, not because any consumer was wrong. WHICH FUNCTION, and why NOT now_dual(): resolve_trading_day(calendar_date) is 'the most recent NYSE trading day ON OR BEFORE this date'; now_dual().trading_day is 'the last trading day fully CLOSED at this instant'. For a Friday-afternoon manual run those disagree (Friday vs Thursday), and every downstream normalizer uses resolve_trading_day - so now_dual() here would open a THIRD partition on exactly the runs hardest to reason about. WHY THIS LAMBDA: InitializeInput is a Pass and States intrinsics carry no NYSE calendar. alpha-engine-weekly-preflight is REUSED rather than a new function created - it already exists, already pins nousergon-lib, and already has a deploy workflow (deploy-weekly-preflight.yml) so this reaches AWS on merge; a NEW Lambda would need an IAM role bootstrap, which is an operator step a PR cannot perform. The action=resolve_run_dates fast path returns before the preflight's first AWS call, and the real WeeklyPreflight invocation passes no action and is byte-identical to before. PLACEMENT: after the run-day gate (pure calendar math, which must stay on $.calendar_date) and before CheckRunMode, so every path that does real work passes through it while the pre-gate Succeed-skip pays for no Lambda it will not use. FAIL-OPEN, and never silent: the Catch routes to NormalizeRunDatesDegraded, which leaves $.run_date at the calendar value and run_date_family at 'calendar_date'. A date normalizer that halts the weekly run is a worse defect than the split it fixes, and the coverage sweep unions BOTH partitions until the 2026-09-05 cutover, so the fallback is covered rather than hidden. TIMEOUT: 30s, deliberately below the Lambda's own ceiling so the SF timeout is the one that binds. | alpha-engine-config-I8809: PARTITION FAMILY = calendar_date IN, trading_day OUT. This is the state that converts one to the other; it is the only site in the graph that legitimately touches both.
